chunks.title: Orchestrate API Reference
chunks.text:
Orchestrate API Reference

cyware-orchestrate-api-reference-theneo

Orchestrate enables security analysts to gather threat data from multiple sources and automate responses to threats and vulnerabilities through advanced workflows. This leads to faster detection, improved analysis, and efficient management of the security operations lifecycle. For more information, see [Orchestrate Product Documentation](https://techdocs.cyware.com/co/en/index-en.html?contextId=cyware_orchestrate_landing).

The Orchestrate open API allows for programmatic interaction with Orchestrate services, enabling automation and integration with other systems in your environment.

For AI agents and LLM-based discovery, see the [Orchestrate API Reference LLM-friendly API guide](https://orchestrateapi.cyware.com/orchestrate-api-reference/llms.txt).

"}'>
  
  Supported Orchestrate Version: 3.5.5.0 and later versions.


The API reference includes public Orchestrate API endpoints for the following modules:

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text:
Authentication

authentication

Users with access to Cyware Orchestrate's Open APIs module can generate the credentials for API authentication.

Generate Open API Credentials
-----------------------------

You can generate open API credentials in the Orchestrate application to access the open API endpoints. For more information on how to generate Open API credentials in Orchestrate, see [Configure Open API](https://techdocs.cyware.com/co/en/configure-open-api.html).

### Mandatory Query Parameters for Requests

After you have generated open API credentials, use them to authenticate your API requests. Ensure the following parameters are included in the query of each request:

*   **Access ID**: Indicates the access ID linked to your Orchestrate Open API. For example, 57d008xx-7xxx-xx-b27a-1feb943d0xxx.
    
*   **Expires**: Indicates the validity of the signature parameter. The signature becomes invalid if not used within the specified expiry duration. You can use `expires = current time + 30 seconds` for authentication. You can specify a margin of 10 to 30 seconds for expiration.
    
*   **Signature**: Signature is a combination of the access ID, secret key, and expiration parameters to authenticate API requests…

chunks.title: Integrations
chunks.text:
Integrations

integrations

Cyware Orchestrate offers a robust App Store with a comprehensive library of apps required to integrate, orchestrate, and respond using various security tools within your organization. These integrations support tasks like threat data collection, prioritization, and other analytics, enabling a holistic approach to orchestration from a unified platform. For more information, see [Apps](https://techdocs.cyware.com/co/en/apps.html##).

You can perform the following actions in this module:

*   **Retrieve App and Instance Details**: Fetch details of available apps and instances, including details of a specific app and instance.
    
*   **Test Instance Connectivity**: Verify the connectivity of a specific app instance to ensure successful integration.
    
*   **Retrieve App Actions and Details**: Fetch a list of actions associated with an app and detailed information about each action.
    
*   **Execute App Actions**: Run specific actions of an app.
    
*   **Download App Package**: Download the ZIP file for a specific app to enable offline access.
    
*   **Install Custom Apps**: Add new custom applications by uploading and installing app packages.

chunks.title: Get Apps
chunks.text:
Get Apps

integrations > get-apps

GET v1/integrations/apps/

Returns a list of apps from My Apps in Orchestrate.

Query parameters:
- q (optional, string): Pass a value for q to search for apps matching the query string.
- ordering (optional, string): Use `ordering=title` to sort by title or `ordering=modified_at` to sort by the last update date. Add `-` before the parameter to sort in descending order.
- page (optional, integer): Pass the page number to retrieve the apps list.
- page_size (optional, integer): Pass the number of items to retrieve per page.
- created_by (optional, string): Pass the user ID to retrieve a list of the apps created by a user.
- app_type (optional, string): Pass `READY_TO_USE` to list active apps, `IN_PROGRESS` to list the inactive apps, and `INSTALLED` to retrieve apps that are installed.
- categories (optional, string): Pass the categories to filter apps.
- is_system (optional, boolean): Pass false to retrieve custom apps or true to retrieve apps.
- is_configured (optional, boolean): Pass true to get configured apps or false to get non-configured apps.
- lite_enabled (optional, boolean): Pass true to retrieve agent-compatible apps or false to fetch apps that are not agent-compatible.
- created_at (optional, string): Pass the `created_at` value to filter apps created in the last week, month, or year.
- created_at__gte (optional, string): Pass the start time in Unix time format. The list of apps created after the entered time will be returned. Example: *1655145000*.
- created_at__lte (optional, string): Pass the end time in Unix time format. The list of apps created before the entered time will be returned. Example: *1642530599*.

chunks.title: Get App Details
chunks.text:
Get App Details

integrations > get-app-details

GET v1/integrations/apps/{app_unique_id}/

Returns the details of a specific app.

Path parameters:
- app_unique_id (required, string): Enter the unique ID of the app to retrieve its details.
You can retrieve the unique IDs of apps using the **Get Apps** endpoint.

chunks.title: Get App Instances
chunks.text:
Get App Instances

integrations > list-app-instances

GET v1/integrations/app-instances/

Retrieves a list of available instances for all apps. To retrieve instances of a specific app, pass the unique ID of the app.

Query parameters:
- page (optional, integer): Pass the page number to retrieve the app details.
- page_size (optional, integer): Pass the number of records to display per page.
- app_unique_id (optional, string): Pass the app unique ID to retrieve the instances of the app. You can retrieve the unique ID of an app using the **Get Apps** endpoint. 
If the app ID is not passed, all available instances will be retrieved.

chunks.title: Create App Instance
chunks.text:
Create App Instance

integrations > create-app-instance

POST v1/integrations/app-instances/

Create an instance in a specific app.

Body fields:
- is_default (optional, boolean): Pass true to set the instance as default.
- title (required, string): Paas a title for the app instance.
- description (optional, string): Pass a description for the app instance.
- app_unique_id (required, string): Pass the unique ID of the app to create an instance. You can retrieve the unique IDs of apps using the **Get Apps** endpoint.
- configuration (optional, object): Pass the necessary configurations to create an instance. The required parameters vary depending on the app.
- version_slug (optional, string): Pass the version of the app to create an instance. For example, *1.0.0*.
You can retrieve the supported version using the **Get Apps** endpoint.
- expiry_date (optional, string): Pass the expiry date of the app instance in ISO format.

chunks.title: Get App Instance Details
chunks.text:
Get App Instance Details

integrations > get-app-instance-details

GET v1/integrations/apps-instances/{instance_id}/

Returns the details of a specific instance.

Path parameters:
- instance_id (required, string): Pass the unique ID of the instance to retrieve details of the app instance. 
Example: *d6a03423-52fd-479b-a79d-85102e53861*.
You can retrieve the instance ID using the **Get App Instances** endpoint.

chunks.title: Test App Instance Connectivity
chunks.text:
Test App Instance Connectivity

integrations > test-app-instance-connectivity

GET v1/integrations/apps-instances/test-connectivity/{instance_id}/

Verify the connectivity of an app instance.

Path parameters:
- instance_id (required, string): Enter the unique ID of the instance to test the connectivity. 
Example: *d6a03423-52fd-479b-a79d-85102e53861f*.
You can retrieve the instance ID using the **Get App Instances** endpoint.

chunks.title: Get App Actions
chunks.text:
Get App Actions

integrations > get-app-actions

GET v1/integrations/app-actions/

Returns a list of all available actions from all apps. To retrieve actions of a specific app, pass the Unique ID of the app.

Query parameters:
- app_unique_id (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the app to retrieve the list of actions. Example: *f8f6af0e-35c8-48e3-8cda-d0fe61476441*. You can retrieve the unique ID of an app using the **Get Apps** endpoint.
- page (optional, string): Pass the page number to retrieve the app actions list.
- page_size (optional, string): Pass the number of items to view per page.

chunks.title: Get Action Details
chunks.text:
Get Action Details

integrations > get-action-details

GET v1/integrations/app-actions/{action_id}/

Returns the details of a specific action.

Path parameters:
- action_id (required, string): Pass the unique ID of the action to retrieve the action details. 
Example: *52091b28-5daa-42f3-9eb9-926994a91ca5*.
You can retrieve unique ID of an action using the **Get App Actions** endpoint.

chunks.title: Execute Action
chunks.text:
Execute Action

integrations > execute-action

POST v1/integrations/actions/execute/

Execute an app action by passing the required parameters in the payload.

Body fields:
- app_identifier (required, string): Pass the identifier of the app. For example, *abuse_ipdb*. You can use the **Get Apps** endpoint to retrieve the identifier of an app.
- action_identifier (required, string): Pass the unique identifier of the action. For example, *check_ip_address*. You can use the **Get App Actions** endpoint to retrieve the identifier of an action.
- action_params (required, object): Pass the parameters required to execute the action. You can retrieve the details of the required parameters of the action using the **Get Action Details** endpoint.
- app_instance_slug (required, string): Pass the resource identifier of the app instance to execute an action. You can retrieve the identifier of an instance using the **Get App Instances** endpoint.

chunks.title: Download App Package
chunks.text:
Download App Package

integrations > download-app-package

GET v1/integrations/apps/download/{app_slug}/

Download the app's ZIP file by entering the app identifier. You can save the response as a ZIP file to your device.

Path parameters:
- app_slug (optional, string): Pass the app's unique resource identifier to generate a downloadable response file.
Example: *abuse_ipdb_1_1_0*.
You can retrieve the app slug of an app using the **Get Apps** endpoint.

chunks.title: Install Custom Apps
chunks.text:
Install Custom Apps

integrations > install-custom-apps

POST v1/integrations/apps/import/

Install custom apps on the Orchestrate application.

Body fields:
- module (required, file): Upload the app package in ZIP format to install the app.

chunks.title: Playbooks
chunks.text:
Playbooks

playbook

Playbooks are a structured sequence of actions organized into workflows to automate and orchestrate security responses, standardizing processes for effective incident and threat management. Orchestrate offers manual and automated playbooks to meet your organization's specific needs.

Playbooks can be scheduled based on application input sources or automatically triggered by specific events. Additionally, playbooks facilitate seamless integration between different security tools, creating a more connected and efficient security environment. For more information, see [Playbooks](https://techdocs.cyware.com/co/en/playbooks.html).

You can perform the following actions in this module:

*   **Export Playbook**: Export playbook details for backup or external use.
    
*   **Retrieve Playbooks and Details**: Fetch the list of playbooks and specific playbook details.
    
*   **Retrieve Playbook Run Logs and Run Details**: Fetch the list of playbook results, run logs, and specific run log details.
    
*   **Execute and Manage Playbooks**: Run or terminate specific playbooks.
    
*   **Download Playbook and Node Results**: Fetch and download results of a specific playbook or a specific no…

chunks.title: Get Playbooks
chunks.text:
Get Playbooks

playbook > open-playbook

GET v1/playbook/

Returns a list of active playbooks in Orchestrate.

Query parameters:
- page (optional, integer): Pass the page number to retrieve the playbook list.
- page_size (optional, integer): Pass the number of items to retrieve per page.
- scheduled (optional, boolean): Pass true or false to filter playbooks based on their scheduled status.
- labels (optional, string): Pass label names to filter playbooks.
- tags (optional, string): Pass the tags to filter the playbooks.
- apps (optional, string): Pass the `app_identifier` of the app. You can retrieve the `app_identifier` of apps using the **Get Apps** endpoint.
- actions (optional, string): Pass the `action_identifier` identifier of the app action. You can retrieve the `action_identifier` of actions using the **Get App Actions** endpoint.
- is_active (optional, boolean): Pass true for active playbooks and false for inactive playbooks.
- modified (optional, string): Pass the last modified value to filter playbooks based on their last modified time.

chunks.title: Get Playbook Details
chunks.text:
Get Playbook Details

playbook > get-playbook

GET v1/playbook/filter/

Returns playbook details based on the playbook ID passed. If no ID is passed, it returns the complete list of both user-created and system playbooks.

Query parameters:
- page (optional, integer): Pass the page number to retrieve the list of playbooks.
- page_size (optional, integer): Pass the number of items to retrieve per page.
- scheduled (optional, boolean): Pass true to retrieve playbooks that are scheduled.
- tags (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the tags to retrieve playbooks.
- labels (optional, string): Pass the label name to retrieve playbooks.
- apps (optional, string): Pass the app identifier. You can retrieve the app identifier using the **Get Apps** endpoint.
- actions (optional, string): Pass the action identifier of an action. You can retrieve the action identifier using the **Get App Actions** endpoint.
- is_active (optional, boolean): Pass true to filter active playbooks, else false.
- modified (optional, string): Pass the last modified value to filter playbooks based on their last modified time.

Body fields:
- unique_id (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of a playbook to retrieve details of a specific playbook. You can retrieve unique IDs of playbook using the **Get Playbooks** endpoint.

chunks.title: Get Playbook Result
chunks.text:
Get Playbook Result

playbook > get-playbook-result

GET v1/playbook/playbook-result/filter/

Returns the playbook runlogs based on the unique ID of the playbook. If no payload is passed, it returns the complete list of playbook run logs.

Query parameters:
- page (optional, integer): Pass the page number to retrieve the playbook result.
- page_size (optional, integer): Pass the number of items to retrieve per page.
- playbook (optional, string): Pass the playbook's unique ID. You can retrieve unique IDs of playbooks using the **Get Playbooks** endoint.

chunks.title: Get Playbook Run Logs
chunks.text:
Get Playbook Run Logs

playbook > list-playbook-run-logs

GET v1/playbook/playbook-result/

Retrieves the list of playbook run logs along with the associated playbook data.

Query parameters:
- page (optional, integer): Pass the page number to retrieve the playbook run logs
- page_size (optional, integer): Pass the number of items to retrieve per page.
- playbook_status (optional, string): Pass the status of the playbook to retrieve the run logs.
- status (optional, string): Pass the playbook run status to filter playbooks.
- source_playbook_result__is_null (optional, boolean): Pass true or false to filter playbooks based on the master playbook.
- apps_list (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the app. You can retrieve the unique ID of an app using the **Get Apps** endpoint.
- playbook (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the playbook. You can retrieve the unique ID of a playbook using the **Get Playbooks** endpoint.
- actions_list (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the app action. You can retrieve the unique ID of an action using the **Get App Actions** endpoint.
- ran_by (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the user who initiated the playbook run.
- scheduled (optional, boolean): Pass true to retrieve scheduled playbooks run logs, else false.
- run_at (optional, string): Pass the date to retrieve playbooks based on the playbook last run.
- run_at__lte (optional, string): Pass the end time in Unix time format to retrieve the playbook run logs.
- run_at__gte (optional, string): Pass the start time in Unix time format to retrieve the playbook run logs.
- ordering (optional, string): Pass the ordering values, such as `modified`, `execution_time`, and `created` to filter playbooks.

chunks.title: Get Playbook Run Log Details
chunks.text:
Get Playbook Run Log Details

playbook > get-playbook-detail-run-log

GET v1/playbook/playbook-result/{playbook_result_unique_id}/

Returns run logs of a specific playbook.

Path parameters:
- playbook_result_unique_id (required, string): Pass the unique ID generated during the playbook run. You can retrieve the unique ID of a run log using the **Get Playbook Run Logs** endpoint.

chunks.title: Get Node Result Details
chunks.text:
Get Node Result Details

playbook > get-node-result-details

GET v1/playbook/node-results/{node_unique_id}/

Returns the details of a specific node.

Path parameters:
- node_unique_id (optional, String): Pass the unique ID of the node. You can retrieve the unique ID of a node using the **Get Playbook Run Log Details** endpoint.

chunks.title: Run Playbook
chunks.text:
Run Playbook

playbook > run-playbook

POST v1/playbook/run/

Run a playbook by passing the playbook unique ID through the payload.

Body fields:
- playbook_unique_id (required, string): Pass the unique ID of the playbook. You can retrieve the unique ID of a playbook using the **Get Playbooks** endpoint.
- data (optional, object): Pass the data or inputs as key-value pairs to run the playbook.
- event (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the event to fetch the event data for playbook execution. You can retrieve the unique IDs of events using the **Get Source Events** endpoint.
- runLog (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the run log to fetch the run log data of playbook execution. You can retrieve the playbook result's unique ID using the **Get Playbook Run Logs** endpoint.
- email_notification_details (optional, object): Pass the email addresses to receive notifications when input is required to proceed with the playbook run. Provide a JSON containing `from_email`, `user_emails`, and `redirect_url` to notify external users.

chunks.title: Export Playbook
chunks.text:
Export Playbook

playbook > export-playbook

GET v1/playbook/export/{playbook_unique_id}/

Returns the export of a playbook in JSON format.

Path parameters:
- playbook_unique_id (required, string): Pass the unique ID of the playbook to export. You can retrieve the unique ID of a playbook using the **Get Playbooks** endpoint.

Query parameters:
- AccessID (optional, string): The Access ID is used to authenticate the Cyware Orchestrate API endpoint.
- Expires (optional, string): This parameter is used to define an expiry time for the API call.
- Signature (optional, string): The Signature is used to authenticate the Cyware Orchestrate API endpoint.

chunks.title: Download Playbook Result
chunks.text:
Download Playbook Result

playbook > playbook-result-download

GET v1/playbook/playbook-result/export/{playbook_result_unique_id}/

Download the input data of the playbook. This endpoint is used to download large files.

Path parameters:
- playbook_result_unique_id (required, string): Pass the unique ID of the `playbook_result` to download the result. You can retrieve the unique ID of a `playbook_result` using the **Get Playbook Run Logs** endpoint.

Query parameters:
- field (required, string): Pass the column name for which the file will be generated. You can retrieve the column name in the `splitted_columns` field of the **Get Playbook Result** endpoint.

chunks.title: Download Node Result
chunks.text:
Download Node Result

playbook > node-result-download

GET v1/playbook/node-results/export/{node_result_unique_id}/

Download the input data or output data of a playbook node. This endpoint is used to download large files.

Path parameters:
- node_result_unique_id (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the node to download the result. You can retrieve the unique ID of a node using the **Get Playbook Run Log Details** endpoint.

Query parameters:
- field (optional, string): Pass the column name for which the file will be generated. The column name can be found in the `splitted_columns` field of the **Get Node Result Details** endpoint.

chunks.title: Bulk Terminate Playbook Runs
chunks.text:
Bulk Terminate Playbook Runs

playbook > bulk-terminate-api-view

POST v1/playbook/playbook-result/bulk-terminate/

Terminate playbook runs in bulk. You can terminate a maximum of 100 playbook runs at a time with the run status in progress, in-queue, waiting, or on hold.

Body fields:
- playbook_result_unique_ids (required, array): Pass the unique IDs of the playbook runs in a list. You can retrieve the unique IDs of playbook results using the **Get Playbook Run Logs** endpoint.

chunks.title: Custom Email Templates
chunks.text:
Custom Email Templates

custom-templates

Email templates are predefined email layouts with a header and body in rich text format. Analysts can reuse and customize these templates, reducing the effort required to compose emails from scratch.

These templates can be used in playbooks to automate email notifications. They are compatible with applications that support Rich Text Format fields, such as the Cyware Email Service - Send Email in Rich Text Format action and more. For more information, see [Email Templates](https://orchestrateapi.cyware.com/custom-templates).

You can perform the following actions in this module:

*   **Get Custom Email Template List:** Retrieve a list of available email templates.
    
*   **Get Custom Email Template Details:** Retrieve detailed information about a specific email template.

chunks.title: Get Custom Email Template List
chunks.text:
Get Custom Email Template List

custom-templates > custom-template-list

GET v1/custom-templates/

Returns the list of custom email templates.

Query parameters:
- page (optional, integer): Pass the page number to retrieve the templates list.
- page_size (optional, integer): Pass the number of items to retrieve per page.
- q (optional, string): Pass a value to q to search for custom templates. You can search email templates using the title.

chunks.title: Get Custom Email Template Details
chunks.text:
Get Custom Email Template Details

custom-templates > custom-template-detail

GET v1/custom-templates/{unique_id}/

Returns details of a specific custom email template.

Path parameters:
- unique_id (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the custom template. You can retrieve the unique ID of a custom email template using the **Get Custom Template List** endpoint.

chunks.title: Code Snippets
chunks.text:
Code Snippets

code-snippets

Code snippets are reusable blocks of code, such as functions, loops, and conditional statements. They support the creation of custom nodes, including custom actions and conditions, within playbooks.

Analysts can leverage a centralized library of reusable code to streamline workflows and reduce effort. This allows them to customize code pieces that are used in multiple playbook workflows from one location. For more information, see [Code Snippets](https://techdocs.cyware.com/co/en/code-snippets.html).

You can perform the following actions in this module:

*   **Retrieve Code Snippets**: Retrieve a list of available code snippets.
    
*   **Retrieve Code Snippet Details**: Fetch detailed information about a specific code snippet.

chunks.title: Get Code Snippets List
chunks.text:
Get Code Snippets List

code-snippets > code-snippets-list

GET v1/code-snippets/

Returns the list of code snippets.

Query parameters:
- page (optional, integer): Pass the page number to retrieve the code snippets list.
- page_size (optional, integer): Pass the number of items to retrieve  per page.
- q (optional, string): Pass the title to search for a code snippet.

chunks.title: Get Code Snippet Details
chunks.text:
Get Code Snippet Details

code-snippets > code-snippets-detail

GET v1/code-snippets/{unique_id}/

Returns details of a specific code snippet.

Path parameters:

chunks.title: Persistent List
chunks.text:
Persistent List

persistent-list

Persistent List is a collection of key-value pairs that analysts can use to store data and then look up from this data to use in a playbook or playbook node. Data stored in a persistent list can survive system reboots, system crashes, and more. Analysts can then retrieve the data defined in a persistent list using any playbook node. For more information, see [Persistent List](https://techdocs.cyware.com/co/en/persistent-list.html).

You can perform the following actions in this module:

*   **Retrieve Persistent Lists and Details**: Fetch a list of all persistent storage objects and fetch detailed information about a specific object using its unique identifier.
    
*   **Create and Update Persistent Lists**: Create new persistent storage objects or modify existing ones to update their details.
    
*   **Delete Persistent Storage Objects**: Remove a specific persistent storage object from Orchestrate.
    
*   **Retrieve Persistent List Slugs**: Get a list of unique resource identifiers for all persistent lists.
    
*   **Retrieve Playbooks Associated with a Persistent List**: Get details and count of playbooks associated with a specific persistent storage object.

chunks.title: Get Persistent Lists
chunks.text:
Get Persistent Lists

persistent-list > persistent-lists

Returns a list of persistent lists.

Query parameters:

- page_size (optional, integer): Pass the number of items to retrieve per page.

chunks.title: Get Persistent List Details

Get Persistent List Details

chunks.title: Create a Persistent List

Update a Persistent List

chunks.title: Delete Persistent Storage Object
chunks.text:
Delete Persistent Storage Object

persistent-list > delete-persistent-storage-object

Delete a persistent list by passing the unique ID. You can delete the persistent list only if it is not used in a playbook. A successful request returns a 200 status code, else the response includes a `non_field_error` object.

Path parameters:
- persistent_storage_unique_id (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the persistent list to retrieve the details. You can retrieve the unique ID of a persistent list using the **Get Persistent Lists** endpoint.

Body fields:

chunks.title: Analytics
chunks.text:
Analytics

analytics

The Analytics Dashboard in Orchestrate provides an overview of activities across modules. Upon signing in, users can view dashboards that offer insights into playbook workflows, app performance, instance usage, and action execution. By analyzing key metrics such as frequently used playbooks and actions, analysts can optimize workflows and enhance automation. Dashboards also help identify underutilized events, diagnose execution errors, and refine automated responses, reducing manual intervention. For more information, see [Analytics Dashboard](https://techdocs.cyware.com/co/en/analytics-dashboard.html).

You can perform the following actions in this module:

*   **Retrieve Playbook Execution Metrics**: Get insights on playbook run count, most active playbooks, and average playbook execution time.
    
*   **Retrieve App and Instance Usage Metrics**: Get insights into the most used and most active apps, instances, and actions.
    
*   **Retrieve Event Processing Metrics**: Get insights on event count, unprocessed events, events with errors, and incoming source events.

chunks.title: Events
chunks.text:
Events

events

A Source Event acts as a trigger for a playbook to execute. You can configure triggers to automatically trigger the execution of a playbook based on the occurrence of an event. These events can occur in Orchestrate or on external platforms such as Respond, Intel Exchange, Splunk, and more. You can configure the source event app and source event type to execute pre-configured playbook workflows. For more information, see [Events](https://techdocs.cyware.com/co/en/labels,-triggers,-and-events.html#labels--triggers--and-events).

When a Source Event is triggered in Cyware Orchestrate, it carries the Source Event Data from integrated tools like Splunk, Respond, and other apps. This data is transmitted in JSON format via the Cyware Orchestrate REST API.

### Authorization

These APIs require an OpenAPI access ID and a generated secret key for authentication.

You can perform the following actions in this module:

*   **Create Events**: Create new events with either detailed or concise response data.
    
*   **Retrieve Source Events and Details**: Fetch a list of all source events and retrieve the details of a specific event.
    
*   **Configure and Manage Events**: Configure events by…

chunks.title: Create Event
chunks.text:
Create Event

events > create-event

POST v1/events/

Create an event by passing the app identifier, action identifier, and data through the payload.

Body fields:
- title (required, string): Pass the title of the event.
- app_identifier (required, string): Pass the source app for the event.
- action_identifier (required, string): Pass the event type for the event.
- extra_data (optional, object): Pass any extra data to be passed with the event.
- data (optional, object): Pass the data in key-value pairs to be passed with the event.

chunks.text:

events > create-event-v2

POST v2/events/

Create an event by passing the app identifier, action identifier, and data through the payload. This endpoint provides a concise response with key parameters.



> [!NOTE]
> This API is available in Orchestrate v3.5.9 onwards.

Body fields:
- title (required, string): Pass the title of the event.
- app_identifier (required, string): Pass a source app for the event.
- action_identifier (required, string): Pass the event type.
- extra_data (optional, object): Pass any extra data as key-value pairs with the event.
- data (optional, object): Pass data as key-value pairs to include with the event.

chunks.title: Get Events
chunks.text:
Get Events

events > list-source-events

GET v1/events/

Returns the list of triggered events.

Query parameters:
- title (optional, string): Pass the keyword to search for in the titles of triggered events.
- app_identifier (optional, string): Pass the source app to filter events based on the apps.
- action_identifier (optional, string): Pass the event type to filter events based on the type of the event.
- q (optional, string): Pass the keyword to search in title (event title), `app_identifier` (source app), `action_identifer` (event type) and `unique_id` (event ID).
- unique_id (optional, string): Pass the unique ID of the event.
- page (optional, integer): Pass the page number to retrieve the source event list.
- page_size (optional, integer): Pass the number of items to retrieve per page.
- labels (optional, string): Pass the label name to filter the results.
- create__lte (optional, string): Pass the custom date in Unix timestamp format. The list of source events modified earlier than the entered time will be returned. Example: *1655231399*.
- created__gte (optional, string): Pass the custom date in Unix timestamp format. The list of source events modified after the entered time will be returned. Example: *1655145000*.
- created (optional, string): Pass the values for the time duration to view source events.

chunks.title: Tags
chunks.text:
Tags

tags

A playbook tag can be used to define role-based access control (RBAC) for playbooks. To configure RBAC, analysts must create playbook tags and associate them with both playbooks and user groups in Respond. Members of a Respond user group can execute playbooks only if the assigned tags match those of the user group. For more information, see [Create Playbook Tags](https://techdocs.cyware.com/co/en/create-playbook-tags.html).

You can perform the following actions in this module:

*   **Retrieve Tags**: Fetch the list of tags.
    
*   **Retrieve Tag Details**: Fetch the details of a specific tag.

chunks.text:

tags > get-list-of-tags

Returns the list of tags.

Query parameters:
- page (optional, string): Pass the page number to retrieve the tags list.
- page_size (optional, string): Pass the number of items to retrieve per page.
- modified__gte (optional, string): Pass the custom date in Unix timestamp format. Returns a list of tags modified after the specified time.
- modified__lte (optional, string): Pass the custom date in Unix timestamp format. Returns a list of tags modified before the specified time.
- ordering (optional, string): Pass a sorting option to filter tags based on it. For example: *title*.
- modified (optional, string): Pass the last modified value to filter tags.

chunks.title: Get Tag Details
chunks.text:

Returns the details of a specific tag.

Path parameters:

chunks.title: Webhooks
chunks.text:
Webhooks

webhooks

Webhooks are serialized messages/information sent from one application to another's unique URL over the web. Webhooks enable analysts to bypass data exchange complications by generating token-based URLs and authenticating endpoints whenever events (GET and POST requests) are triggered in the Orchestrate application.

**Webhooks** module allows users to create and manage webhook configurations and tokens. Users will be able to access features based on the permissions assigned to the user in the Orchestrate application. For more information, see [Configure Webhooks](https://techdocs.cyware.com/co/en/configure-webhooks.html).

Authentication
--------------

These APIs require a webhook token as a mandatory parameter.

#### Generate Webhook Credentials

1.  Navigate to the **Admin Panel** and select **Webhooks**.
    
2.  Click **Add Webhook** and enter the webhook details.
    
3.  After entering the details, click **Generate Webhook URL**.
    
4.  After the webhook URL is generated, copy the **token** and the **Base URL** displayed to you, and then configure the keys in the required application.
    

You can perform the following actions in this module:

*   **Test Connectivity**: …

chunks.title: Test connectivity
chunks.text:
Test connectivity

webhooks > test-connectivity

GET {webhook_url}/test_connectivity/

Use this API to test the connectivity.

Path parameters:
- webhook_url (required, String): Pass the webhook URL retrieved from Orchestrate application.

Query parameters:
- token (required, string): Pass the webhooks authentication token generated in Cyware Orchestrate. For example, ab1929a2-7d56-4511-b130-a5c3b6592702.

chunks.title: Create Event
chunks.text:
Create Event

webhooks > create-event

POST {webhook_url}/{app-identifier}/{action-identifier}/

Creates an event by passing the app identifier and action identifier through the URL and data through the payload.



> [!NOTE]
> Note: Starting from Orchestrate v3.5.9, the webhook URLs generated in the Orchestrate platform are updated to provide concise responses with key parameters such as title, readable_id, source, and more. To retrieve a detailed response, remove the /v2 from the webhook URL. The following is the example webhook URL that retrieves the detailed response: https:///soarapi/webhooks_auth/events/?token=1df121212-121x-1212-3434-a67823232356.

Path parameters:
- webhook_url (required, String): Pass the webhook URL retrieved from the Orchestrate application.
- app-identifier (required, string): Pass the source app to create an event.
- action-identifier (required, string): Enter the event type to create an event.

Query parameters:
- token (required, string): Pass the webhook token retrieved from the Orchestrate application.

Body fields:
- data (required, string): Pass the data for action execution.
- title (optional, string): Pass a title for the event.
- labels (optional, string): Pass labels for the events.  
To view the list of labels, sign in Orchestrate and go to Triggers > Labels.
